passages.text: Then Jesus said to them, “Truly I tell you, there are some standing here who will not taste death before they see the kingdom of God arrive with power.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He said, “I tell you the truth.
Some people are standing here now.
These people will not die before they see something happen.
They will see the kingdom of God come with power.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι εἰσίν τινες ὧδε τῶν ἑστηκότων οἵτινες οὐ μὴ γεύσωνται θανάτου ἕως ἂν ἴδωσιν τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐληλυθυῖαν ἐν δυνάμει

passages.text: After six days Jesus took with Him Peter, James, and John, and led them up a high mountain by themselves. There He was transfigured before them.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of Man.
Six days passed.
Jesus chose Peter, James, and John.
Jesus took Peter, James, and John with Him.
Jesus led them up a high mountain.
No one else was with them.
They were alone together.
Jesus changed in appearance in front of them.
Jesus was transfigured before Peter, James, and John.
passages.original: Καὶ μετὰ ἡμέρας ἓξ παραλαμβάνει ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὸν Πέτρον καὶ τὸν Ἰάκωβον καὶ τὸν Ἰωάννην καὶ ἀναφέρει αὐτοὺς εἰς ὄρος ὑψηλὸν κατ’ ἰδίαν μόνους καὶ μετεμορφώθη ἔμπροσθεν αὐτῶν

passages.text: His clothes became radiantly white, brighter than any launderer on earth could bleach them.
passages.sermon:
Jesus stood before Peter, James, and John.
His clothes changed.
His clothes became very bright.
His clothes became extremely white.
No launderer on earth can make clothes that white.
passages.original: καὶ τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ ἐγένετο στίλβοντα λευκὰ λίαν οἷα γναφεὺς ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς οὐ δύναται οὕτως λευκᾶναι

passages.text: And Elijah and Moses appeared before them, talking with Jesus.
passages.sermon:
Jesus stood on the mountain.
Peter, James, and John were with Him.
Elijah appeared to them.
Moses also appeared to them.
Elijah and Moses talked with Jesus.
passages.original: καὶ ὤφθη αὐτοῖς Ἠλίας σὺν Μωϋσεῖ καὶ ἦσαν συλλαλοῦντες τῷ Ἰησοῦ

passages.text: Peter said to Jesus, “Rabbi, it is good for us to be here. Let us put up three shelters —one for You, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”
passages.sermon:
Peter was one of Jesus’ disciples.
Peter spoke to Jesus.
Peter called Jesus “Rabbi.”
Peter said, “It is good for us to be here.”
Peter suggested building three shelters.
Peter said, “Let us put up three shelters.”
Peter said, “One shelter for You.”
Peter said, “One shelter for Moses.”
Peter said, “One shelter for Elijah.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Πέτρος λέγει τῷ Ἰησοῦ Ῥαββί καλόν ἐστιν ἡμᾶς ὧδε εἶναι καὶ ποιήσωμεν τρεῖς σκηνάς σοὶ μίαν καὶ Μωϋσεῖ μίαν καὶ Ἠλίᾳ μίαν

passages.text: For they were all so terrified that Peter did not know what else to say.
passages.sermon:
Peter stood with Jesus, Moses, and Elijah on the mountain.
Peter and the others felt very afraid.
Peter did not know what to say.
Peter spoke because he was terrified.
passages.original: οὐ γὰρ ᾔδει τί ἀποκριθῇ ἔκφοβοι γὰρ ἐγένοντο

passages.text: Then a cloud appeared and enveloped them, and a voice came from the cloud: “This is My beloved Son. Listen to Him!”
passages.sermon:
A cloud appeared.
The cloud covered them.
A voice spoke from the cloud.
The voice said, “This is My beloved Son.”
The voice said, “Listen to Him.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο νεφέλη ἐπισκιάζουσα αὐτοῖς καὶ ἐγένετο φωνὴ ἐκ τῆς νεφέλης Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ Υἱός μου ὁ ἀγαπητός ἀκούετε αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Suddenly, when they looked around, they saw no one with them except Jesus.
passages.sermon:
Peter, James, and John were on the mountain with Jesus.
They looked around suddenly.
They did not see anyone else with them.
They saw only Jesus with themselves.
passages.original: καὶ ἐξάπινα περιβλεψάμενοι οὐκέτι οὐδένα εἶδον ἀλλὰ τὸν Ἰησοῦν μόνον μεθ’ ἑαυτῶν

passages.text: As they were coming down the mountain, Jesus admonished them not to tell anyone what they had seen until the Son of Man had risen from the dead.
passages.sermon:
Jesus walked down the mountain with His disciples.
He spoke to them.
He gave them a command.
He told them not to tell anyone what they had seen.
He said they must wait.
He said they could speak only after the Son of Man had risen from the dead.
passages.original: Καὶ καταβαινόντων αὐτῶν ἐκ τοῦ ὄρους διεστείλατο αὐτοῖς ἵνα μηδενὶ ἃ εἶδον διηγήσωνται εἰ μὴ ὅταν ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστῇ

passages.text: So they kept this matter to themselves, discussing what it meant to rise from the dead.
passages.sermon:
The disciples heard Jesus speak about rising from the dead.
They did not tell anyone about what they had seen.
They kept this matter private among themselves.
They talked with each other about what it means to rise from the dead.
passages.original: καὶ τὸν λόγον ἐκράτησαν πρὸς ἑαυτοὺς συζητοῦντες τί ἐστιν τὸ ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστῆναι

passages.text: And they asked Jesus, “Why do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?”
passages.sermon:
The disciples spoke to Jesus.
They asked him a question.
They said, “The scribes teach something.”
They said, “The scribes say Elijah must come first.”
passages.original: καὶ ἐπηρώτων αὐτὸν λέγοντες Ὅτι Λέγουσιν οἱ γραμματεῖς ὅτι Ἠλίαν δεῖ ἐλθεῖν πρῶτον

passages.text: He replied, “Elijah does indeed come first, and he restores all things. Why then is it written that the Son of Man must suffer many things and be rejected?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to them.
He said, “Elijah comes first.
Elijah restores all things.
Scripture says the Son of Man must suffer many things.
Scripture says the Son of Man must be rejected.
Why is it written this way about the Son of Man?”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ἔφη αὐτοῖς Ἠλίας μὲν ἐλθὼν πρῶτον ἀποκαθιστάνει πάντα καὶ πῶς γέγραπται ἐπὶ τὸν Υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἵνα πολλὰ πάθῃ καὶ ἐξουδενηθῇ

passages.text: But I tell you that Elijah has indeed come, and they have done to him whatever they wished, just as it is written about him.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He said, “Elijah has already come.
People did to Elijah whatever they wanted.
This happened just as Scripture said about him.”
passages.original: ἀλλὰ λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι καὶ Ἠλίας ἐλήλυθεν καὶ ἐποίησαν αὐτῷ ὅσα ἤθελον καθὼς γέγραπται ἐπ’ αὐτόν

passages.text: When they returned to the other disciples, they saw a large crowd around them, and scribes arguing with them.
passages.sermon:
Jesus, Peter, James, and John returned to the other disciples.
They saw a large crowd gathered around the disciples.
Scribes were present with the crowd.
The scribes were arguing with the disciples.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐλθόντες πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς εἶδον ὄχλον πολὺν περὶ αὐτοὺς καὶ γραμματεῖς συζητοῦντας πρὸς αὐτούς

passages.text: As soon as all the people saw Jesus, they were filled with awe and ran to greet Him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus returned to the disciples.
A large crowd stood around them.
The people saw Jesus.
All the people felt great awe.
They ran to Jesus.
They greeted Him.
passages.original: καὶ εὐθὺς πᾶς ὁ ὄχλος ἰδόντες αὐτὸν ἐξεθαμβήθησαν καὶ προστρέχοντες ἠσπάζοντο αὐτόν

passages.text: “What are you disputing with them?” He asked.
passages.sermon:
Jesus saw a crowd around His disciples.
He saw scribes arguing with them.
Jesus spoke to the people.
He asked a question.
Jesus said, “What are you disputing with them?”
passages.original: Καὶ ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτούς Τί συζητεῖτε πρὸς αὑτούς

passages.text: Someone in the crowd replied, “Teacher, I brought You my son, who has a spirit that makes him mute.
passages.sermon:
A man stood in the crowd.
He spoke to Jesus.
He said, “Teacher, I brought my son to You.
My son has a spirit.
This spirit makes him unable to speak.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἀπεκρίθη αὐτῷ εἷς ἐκ τοῦ ὄχλου Διδάσκαλε ἤνεγκα τὸν υἱόν μου πρὸς σέ ἔχοντα πνεῦμα ἄλαλον

passages.text: Whenever it seizes him, it throws him to the ground. He foams at the mouth, gnashes his teeth, and becomes rigid. I asked Your disciples to drive it out, but they were unable.”
passages.sermon:
A spirit controls my son.
Whenever the spirit seizes him, it throws him down.
He foams at the mouth.
He gnashes his teeth.
He becomes rigid.
I asked your disciples to cast out the spirit.
They could not do it.
passages.original: καὶ ὅπου ἐὰν αὐτὸν καταλάβῃ ῥήσσει αὐτόν καὶ ἀφρίζει καὶ τρίζει τοὺς ὀδόντας καὶ ξηραίνεται καὶ εἶπα τοῖς μαθηταῖς σου ἵνα αὐτὸ ἐκβάλωσιν καὶ οὐκ ἴσχυσαν

passages.text: “O unbelieving generation!” Jesus replied. “How long must I remain with you? How long must I put up with you? Bring the boy to Me.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He called them an unbelieving generation.
He asked, “How long must I stay with you?”
He asked, “How long must I put up with you?”
He told them, “Bring the boy to Me.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς αὐτοῖς λέγει Ὦ γενεὰ ἄπιστος ἕως πότε πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἔσομαι ἕως πότε ἀνέξομαι ὑμῶν φέρετε αὐτὸν πρός με

passages.text: So they brought him, and seeing Jesus, the spirit immediately threw the boy into a convulsion. He fell to the ground and rolled around, foaming at the mouth.
passages.sermon:
They brought the boy to Jesus.
The evil spirit saw Jesus.
The spirit immediately attacked the boy.
The boy fell to the ground.
He rolled around on the ground.
He foamed at the mouth.
passages.original: Καὶ ἤνεγκαν αὐτὸν πρὸς αὐτόν καὶ ἰδὼν αὐτὸν τὸ πνεῦμα εὐθὺς συνεσπάραξεν αὐτόν καὶ πεσὼν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἐκυλίετο ἀφρίζων

passages.text: Jesus asked the boy’s father, “How long has this been with him?” “From childhood,” he said.
passages.sermon:
Jesus saw a boy who suffered from an evil spirit.
Jesus spoke to the boy’s father.
Jesus asked, “How long has your son had this problem?”
The father answered Jesus.
The father said, “He has had this since he was a child.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἐπηρώτησεν τὸν πατέρα αὐτοῦ Πόσος χρόνος ἐστὶν ὡς τοῦτο γέγονεν αὐτῷ Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν Ἐκ παιδιόθεν

passages.text: “It often throws him into the fire or into the water, trying to kill him. But if You can do anything, have compassion on us and help us.”
passages.sermon:
The evil spirit attacks my son.
It tries to destroy him.
It often throws him into the fire.
It often throws him into the water.
It wants to kill him.
If you can do anything, please help us.
Have compassion on us.
passages.original: καὶ πολλάκις καὶ εἰς πῦρ αὐτὸν ἔβαλεν καὶ εἰς ὕδατα ἵνα ἀπολέσῃ αὐτόν ἀλλ’ εἴ τι δύνῃ βοήθησον ἡμῖν σπλαγχνισθεὶς ἐφ’ ἡμᾶς

passages.text: “If You can?” echoed Jesus. “All things are possible to him who believes!”
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to the boy’s father.\r\nJesus said, “If you can?”\r\nJesus said, “All things are possible for the one who believes.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ Τὸ Εἰ δύνῃ πάντα δυνατὰ τῷ πιστεύοντι

passages.text: Immediately the boy’s father cried out, “I do believe; help my unbelief!”
passages.sermon:
The boy’s father spoke to Jesus.
He cried out immediately.
He said, “I do believe.”
He also said, “Help my unbelief.”
passages.original: Εὐθὺς κράξας ὁ πατὴρ τοῦ παιδίου ἔλεγεν Πιστεύω βοήθει μου τῇ ἀπιστίᾳ

passages.text: When Jesus saw that a crowd had come running, He rebuked the unclean spirit. “You deaf and mute spirit,” He said, “I command you to come out and never enter him again.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus saw a crowd running toward Him.
Jesus acted immediately.
Jesus spoke to the unclean spirit.
The unclean spirit made the boy deaf and mute.
Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit.
Jesus said, “You deaf and mute spirit, I command you.”
Jesus commanded the spirit to come out of the boy.
Jesus commanded the spirit never to enter the boy again.
passages.original: Ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὅτι ἐπισυντρέχει ὄχλος ἐπετίμησεν τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἀκαθάρτῳ λέγων αὐτῷ Τὸ ἄλαλον καὶ κωφὸν πνεῦμα ἐγὼ ἐπιτάσσω σοι ἔξελθε ἐξ αὐτοῦ καὶ μηκέτι εἰσέλθῃς εἰς αὐτόν

passages.text: After shrieking and convulsing him violently, the spirit came out. The boy became like a corpse, so that many said, “He is dead.”
passages.sermon:
The unclean spirit shrieked.
The spirit convulsed the boy violently.
The spirit came out of the boy.
The boy looked like a corpse.
Many people saw him.
Many people said, “He is dead.”
passages.original: Καὶ κράξας καὶ πολλὰ σπαράξας ἐξῆλθεν καὶ ἐγένετο ὡσεὶ νεκρὸς ὥστε τοὺς πολλοὺς λέγειν ὅτι ἀπέθανεν

passages.text: But Jesus took him by the hand and helped him to his feet, and he stood up.
passages.sermon:
Jesus saw the boy lying still.
Jesus took the boy’s hand.
Jesus lifted the boy up.
The boy stood up.
passages.original: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς κρατήσας τῆς χειρὸς αὐτοῦ ἤγειρεν αὐτόν καὶ ἀνέστη

passages.text: After Jesus had gone into the house, His disciples asked Him privately, “Why couldn’t we drive it out?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus entered the house.
His disciples were with Him.
The disciples spoke to Jesus in private.
They asked Jesus a question.
They said, “Why couldn’t we drive it out?”
passages.original: Καὶ εἰσελθόντος αὐτοῦ εἰς οἶκον οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ κατ’ ἰδίαν ἐπηρώτων αὐτόν Ὅτι ἡμεῖς οὐκ ἠδυνήθημεν ἐκβαλεῖν αὐτό

passages.text: Jesus answered, “This kind cannot come out, except by prayer.”
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to His disciples.\r\nHe said, “This kind cannot come out by any means except by prayer.”
passages.original: Καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Τοῦτο τὸ γένος ἐν οὐδενὶ δύναται ἐξελθεῖν εἰ μὴ ἐν προσευχῇ

passages.text: Going on from there, they passed through Galilee. But Jesus did not want anyone to know, because He was teaching His disciples. He told them, “The Son of Man will be delivered into the hands of men. They will kill Him, and after three days He will rise.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus and His disciples left that place.
They traveled through Galilee.
Jesus did not want anyone to know where they were.
Jesus wanted to teach His disciples in private.
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He said, “The Son of Man will be handed over to men.
They will kill Him.
After He is killed, He will rise after three days.”
passages.original: Κἀκεῖθεν ἐξελθόντες παρεπορεύοντο διὰ τῆς Γαλιλαίας καὶ οὐκ ἤθελεν ἵνα τις γνοῖ ἐδίδασκεν γὰρ τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς ὅτι Ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδίδοται εἰς χεῖρας ἀνθρώπων καὶ ἀποκτενοῦσιν αὐτόν καὶ ἀποκτανθεὶς μετὰ τρεῖς ἡμέρας ἀναστήσεται

passages.text: But they did not understand this statement, and they were afraid to ask Him about it.
passages.sermon: The disciples did not understand what Jesus said.\r\nThey felt afraid.\r\nThey did not want to ask Jesus about His statement.
passages.original: οἱ δὲ ἠγνόουν τὸ ῥῆμα καὶ ἐφοβοῦντο αὐτὸν ἐπερωτῆσαι

passages.text: Then they came to Capernaum. While Jesus was in the house, He asked them, “What were you discussing on the way?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus traveled with His disciples.
They arrived in Capernaum.
Jesus entered a house with them.
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He asked them a question.
He said, “What were you discussing on the way?”
passages.original: Καὶ ἦλθον εἰς Καφαρναούμ Καὶ ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ γενόμενος ἐπηρώτα αὐτούς Τί ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ διελογίζεσθε

passages.text: But they were silent, for on the way they had been arguing about which of them was the greatest.
passages.sermon:
The disciples did not speak.
They kept silent.
They had argued with each other while they traveled.
They argued about which one of them was the greatest.
passages.original: οἱ δὲ ἐσιώπων πρὸς ἀλλήλους γὰρ διελέχθησαν ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ τίς μείζων

passages.text: Sitting down, Jesus called the Twelve and said, “If anyone wants to be first, he must be the last of all and the servant of all.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus sat down.
He called the Twelve disciples to Him.
He spoke to them.
He said, “If anyone wants to be first, he must be last of all.
He must be the servant of all.”
passages.original: Καὶ καθίσας ἐφώνησεν τοὺς δώδεκα καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Εἴ τις θέλει πρῶτος εἶναι ἔσται πάντων ἔσχατος καὶ πάντων διάκονος

passages.text: Then He had a little child stand among them. Taking the child in His arms, He said to them, “Whoever welcomes one of these little children in My name welcomes Me, and whoever welcomes Me welcomes not only Me, but the One who sent Me.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus took a little child.
He placed the child in the middle of the disciples.
Jesus held the child in His arms.
He spoke to the disciples.
He said, “Whoever welcomes one of these little children in My name welcomes Me.
Whoever welcomes Me does not welcome only Me.
He also welcomes the One who sent Me.”
passages.original: Καὶ λαβὼν παιδίον ἔστησεν αὐτὸ ἐν μέσῳ αὐτῶν καὶ ἐναγκαλισάμενος αὐτὸ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ὃς ἂν ἓν τῶν τοιούτων παιδίων δέξηται ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματί μου ἐμὲ δέχεται καὶ ὃς ἂν ἐμὲ δέχηται οὐκ ἐμὲ δέχεται ἀλλὰ τὸν ἀποστείλαντά με

passages.text: John said to Him, “Teacher, we saw someone else driving out demons in Your name, and we tried to stop him, because he does not accompany us.”
passages.sermon:
John spoke to Jesus.
John called Jesus "Teacher."
John said, "We saw someone else driving out demons."
This person used Your name, Jesus.
This person does not follow us.
We tried to stop him.
We tried to stop him because he does not follow us."
passages.original: Ἔφη αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰωάννης Διδάσκαλε εἴδομέν τινα ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί σου ἐκβάλλοντα δαιμόνια ὃς οὐκ ἀκολουθεῖ ἡμῖν καὶ ἐκωλύομεν αὐτόν ὅτι οὐκ ἠκολούθει ἡμῖν

passages.text: “Do not stop him,” Jesus replied. “For no one who performs a miracle in My name can turn around and speak evil of Me.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He said, “Do not stop him.”
No one can do a miracle in My name and then quickly speak evil of Me.
Anyone who performs a miracle by My authority cannot soon speak against Me.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν Μὴ κωλύετε αὐτόν οὐδεὶς γάρ ἐστιν ὃς ποιήσει δύναμιν ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματί μου καὶ δυνήσεται ταχὺ κακολογῆσαί με

passages.text: For whoever is not against us is for us.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to His disciples.\r\nHe said this about people who do not oppose Him and His followers.\r\nAnyone who is not against us is on our side.
passages.original: ὃς γὰρ οὐκ ἔστιν καθ’ ἡμῶν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἐστιν

passages.text: Indeed, if anyone gives you even a cup of water because you bear the name of Christ, truly I tell you, he will never lose his reward.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus said this about people who help His followers.
If anyone gives you a cup of water because you belong to Christ, that person will receive a reward.
I tell you the truth.
That person will never lose his reward.
passages.original: Ὃς γὰρ ἂν ποτίσῃ ὑμᾶς ποτήριον ὕδατος ἐν ὀνόματι ὅτι Χριστοῦ ἐστε ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐ μὴ ἀπολέσῃ τὸν μισθὸν αὐτοῦ

passages.text: But if anyone causes one of these little ones who believe in Me to stumble, it would be better for him to have a large millstone hung around his neck and to be thrown into the sea.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He referred to "these little ones who believe in Me."
If anyone causes one of these believers to stumble, that person does great harm.
It would be better for that person to have a large millstone tied around his neck.
It would be better for him to be thrown into the sea.
passages.original: Καὶ ὃς ἂν σκανδαλίσῃ ἕνα τῶν μικρῶν τούτων τῶν πιστευόντων εἰς ἐμέ καλόν ἐστιν αὐτῷ μᾶλλον εἰ περίκειται μύλος ὀνικὸς περὶ τὸν τράχηλον αὐτοῦ καὶ βέβληται εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν

passages.text: If your hand causes you to sin, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life crippled than to have two hands and go into hell, into the unquenchable fire.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to His followers.
He warns about sin.
If your hand causes you to sin, cut it off.
It is better for you to enter life crippled.
It is worse to have two hands and go into hell.
Hell is a place of unquenchable fire.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐὰν σκανδαλίζῃ σε ἡ χείρ σου ἀπόκοψον αὐτήν καλόν ἐστίν σε κυλλὸν εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν ζωὴν ἢ τὰς δύο χεῖρας ἔχοντα ἀπελθεῖν εἰς τὴν γέενναν εἰς τὸ πῦρ τὸ ἄσβεστον

passages.text: If your foot causes you to sin, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life lame than to have two feet and be thrown into hell.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to His disciples.
He warns them about sin.
If your foot causes you to sin, cut it off.
It is better for you to enter life lame.
It is better to enter life with only one foot.
It is worse to have two feet and be thrown into hell.
passages.original: καὶ ἐὰν ὁ πούς σου σκανδαλίζῃ σε ἀπόκοψον αὐτόν καλόν ἐστίν σε εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν ζωὴν χωλὸν ἢ τοὺς δύο πόδας ἔχοντα βληθῆναι εἰς τὴν γέενναν

passages.text: And if your eye causes you to sin, pluck it out. It is better for you to enter the kingdom of God with one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into hell, where ‘their worm never dies, and the fire is never quenched.’
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the crowds in Judea, beyond the Jordan.
Jesus taught them as He usually did.
Jesus said, "If your eye causes you to sin, remove it.
It is better to enter the kingdom of God with one eye.
It is worse to have two eyes and be thrown into hell.
In hell, the worm never dies.
In hell, the fire is never quenched."
passages.original: καὶ ἐὰν ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου σκανδαλίζῃ σε ἔκβαλε αὐτόν καλόν σέ ἐστιν μονόφθαλμον εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ ἢ δύο ὀφθαλμοὺς ἔχοντα βληθῆναι εἰς τὴν γέενναν ὅπου Ὁ σκώληξ αὐτῶν οὐ τελευτᾷ καὶ τὸ πῦρ οὐ σβέννυται

passages.text: For everyone will be salted with fire.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to the crowds in Judea.\r\nHe taught them as He usually did.\r\nJesus said, “Everyone will be salted with fire.”
passages.original: Πᾶς γὰρ πυρὶ ἁλισθήσεται

passages.text: Salt is good, but if the salt loses its saltiness, with what will you season it? Have salt among yourselves, and be at peace with one another.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples and the crowds.
He said, “Salt is good.
But salt can lose its saltiness.
If salt loses its saltiness, you cannot make it salty again.
You must have salt in yourselves.
You must live in peace with one another.”
passages.original: καλὸν τὸ ἅλας ἐὰν δὲ τὸ ἅλας ἄναλον γένηται ἐν τίνι αὐτὸ ἀρτύσετε ἔχετε ἐν ἑαυτοῖς ἅλα καὶ εἰρηνεύετε ἐν ἀλλήλοις
